competition_eligible_organizations.note: Organizations with OPP (Organizacja Pożytku Publicznego) status eligible for 1.5% tax donations

shelters.name: Schronisko dla Bezdomnych Zwierząt "Na Paluchu"
shelters.description: Warsaw’s large municipal animal shelter,...by the city, it only takes in stray animals from within Warsaw.

shelters.name: Fundacja Azylu pod Psim Aniołem
shelters.description: Fundacja Azyl helps animals in need, primarily dogs but also other animals requiring assistance. Registered in April 2008, the foundation is a public benefit organization operating in the Łódź region.

shelters.name: Fundacja Schronisko dla Bezdomnych Zwierząt w Józefowie
shelters.description: A private shelter near Warsaw that takes in abandoned dogs and cats, often from difficult intervention cases. Known for its active volunteer base and transparent communication about adoptions and needs.

shelters.name: Fundacja Znajdki
shelters.description: Small shelter and rescue foundation focusing on dogs and cats from Mazovia. Many animals come from intervention cases in rural areas; foundation provides vet care, socialization and finds new homes.

shelters.name: Fundacja Bernardyn
shelters.description: Rescue specializing originally in Saint Bernards, today helping many large-breed dogs. Works with temporary homes around Warsaw and across Poland, prepares dogs for adoption.

organizations.name: Fundacja Międzynarodowy Ruch Na Rzecz Zwierząt "Viva!"
organizations.description: One of the best-known Polish animal rights organizations, active nationwide. Runs campaigns against fur farming, live animal transport and industrial farming, and supports many local initiatives and shelters.

organizations.name: Fundacja Viva! Akcja dla Zwierząt
organizations.focus: Animal rights, anti-fur campaigns, farm animal rescue, Korabiewice sanctuary

organizations.name: Fundacja Przyjaciele Palucha
organizations.focus: Medical care for sick and elderly shelter animals

organizations.name: Fundacja Przyjaciele Palucha
organizations.description: Charity supporting treatment and special care for the most vulnerable animals from Schronisko na Paluchu (seniors, chronic illnesses, complicated surgeries). Financed mostly by 1,5% PIT donations and individual donors.

organizations.name: Stowarzyszenie Ochrony Zwierząt "Grupa Pomocy Zwierzętom"
organizations.description: Grass-roots NGO from Warsaw region running interventions, temporary homes and campaigns for responsible animal guardianship.

organizations.name: Fundacja Koteria
organizations.focus: Urban cats, spay/neuter, colony management

organizations.name: Fundacja Koteria
organizations.description: Runs Warsaw’s only free clinic dedicated to sterilising free-living cats, plus adoption of social cats. Since 2009 has neutered thousands of cats and supports city caretakers with vet care and food.

organizations.name: Fundacja Zwierzęca Polana
organizations.description: Rescue focused mainly on dogs from hard intervention cases and dogs with disabilities (e.g. wheelchair dogs). Provides advanced rehabilitation and behavioural work before adoption.

organizations.name: Stowarzyszenie Pomocy Królikom – Oddział Warszawa
organizations.description: Branch of Poland-wide rabbit rescue that takes in abandoned rabbits and small rodents, provides vet care and finds specialised homes.

organizations.name: Fundacja ARGOS
organizations.description: Foundation known e.g. from managing cat populations in Warsaw (sterilisation programs, feeding sites) and educational work on animal welfare.

organizations.name: Stowarzyszenie Otwarte Klatki
organizations.description: Nation-wide animal rights group exposing cruelty in factory farming and pushing retailers towards better standards. Warsaw is one of its main local groups.

organizations.name: Fundacja Ratujemy Zwierzaki (Ratujemy.pl)
organizations.focus: Supporting animal organizations, grants, equipment

organizations.name: Towarzystwo Opieki nad Zwierzętami w Polsce – Zarząd Główny
organizations.focus: Animal welfare, shelter support, interventions

organizations.name: Fundacja dla Zwierząt Puszatek
organizations.focus: National adoption register, animal rescue

organizations.name: Fundacja Viva! Schronisko w Korabiewicach
organizations.description: Large animal sanctuary under Viva! taking care of dogs, cats and farm animals, including many intervention cases. Although located outside Warsaw, it’s strongly connected with the Warsaw Viva! structures.

organizations.name: Fundacja Animal Rescue Poland
organizations.description: A Warsaw-area emergency rescue group (est. 2015) that helps domestic, farm, and wild animals. Its volunteers run 24/7 interventions for injured wildlife, cruelty cases, and accidents, working closely with police and veterinarians:contentReference[oaicite:9]{index=9}:contentReference[oaicite:10]{index=10}.

organizations.name: Towarzystwo Opieki nad Zwierzętami w Polsce – Oddział Warszawa
organizations.description: The Warsaw branch of Poland’s oldest animal welfare society (TOZ). TOZ chapters rescue thousands of animals and have been instrumental in animal protection laws (they spearheaded the 1997 Animal Protection Act):contentReference[oaicite:14]{index=14}. They promote humane treatment and run adoption and education programs.

organizations.name: Fundacja Pegasus
organizations.description: A rescue foundation saving horses from abuse and slaughter since 2002. Pegasus operates a sanctuary near Warsaw where horses, ponies, donkeys, goats, llamas, as well as some dogs and cats, are rehabilitated and cared for on a 30-hectare farm:contentReference[oaicite:16]{index=16}:contentReference[oaicite:17]{index=17}.

organizations.name: Fundacja Opieki nad Zwierzętami Canis
organizations.description: A Warsaw-based charity (est. 1992) focused on helping stray cats and dogs:contentReference[oaicite:18]{index=18}. CANIS provides vet care (sterilizations, treatments) and runs a network of foster homes and adoption centers to rehome abandoned pets:contentReference[oaicite:19]{index=19}.

organizations.name: Stowarzyszenie Empatia
organizations.description: A Warsaw-based animal rights association founded in 2004 that promotes veganism and respect for all animals through peaceful advocacy and education. Empatia works to advance the humane treatment and legal protection of animals:contentReference[oaicite:21]{index=21}.

shelters.name: KTOZ Schronisko dla Bezdomnych Zwierząt w Krakowie
shelters.description: Municipal shelter run by KTOZ (Krakowskie Towarzystwo Opieki nad Zwierzętami). Takes in dogs and cats from Kraków; intensive adoption and volunteering programmes.

shelters.name: Schronisko dla Bezdomnych Zwierząt w Krakowie
Schronisko dla Bezdomnych Zwierząt w Borku (gmina Zielonki – pod Krakowem)
shelters.description: Shelter cooperating with multiple municipalities around Kraków; takes in many dogs from small villages and runs adoption campaigns in the region.

shelters.name: Schronisko dla Bezdomnych Zwierząt Psie Pole (okolice Krakowa)
shelters.description: Private shelter near Kraków, often taking in difficult cases and long-stay dogs. Cooperates with volunteers from the city.

shelters.name: Schronisko dla Bezdomnych Zwierząt w Chełmku / OTOZ Animals
shelters.description: Shelter run under OTOZ Animals brand; many animals from Małopolska region end up here.

shelters.name: Fundacja Ostoja Cztery Łapy
shelters.description: Fundacja Ostoja Cztery Łapy (Four Paws Haven Foundation) helps homeless animals, particularly cats in the Kraków and Małopolska region. Established in March 2018, the foundation provides rescue, care, and adoption services for abandoned cats.

shelters.name: Schronisko dla Zwierząt w Krakowie – Oddział TOZ
shelters.description: KTOZ’s animal shelter (see above). It is the only municipal shelter in Kraków, taking in stray dogs and cats, and is supported by public donations and 1.5% tax funds:contentReference[oaicite:25]{index=25}.

shelters.name: Centrum adopcyjne "Psie Pole" (Kraków)
shelters.description: A privately-run dog rescue and adoption center near Kraków that provides shelter and care for abandoned dogs and seeks new homes for them. (Operated by a local rescue group; not OPP).

organizations.name: Krakowskie Towarzystwo Opieki nad Zwierzętami (KTOZ)
organizations.description: Historic animal welfare society managing the official municipal shelter in Kraków and running interventions, education and low-cost neutering programmes.

organizations.name: Krakowska Fundacja Pomocy Zwierzętom Stawiamy na Łapy
organizations.focus: Cat rescue, spay/neuter, temporary homes

organizations.name: Stawiamy na Łapy
organizations.description: Very active Kraków-based foundation helping mostly cats (and some dogs) – many temporary homes, large social media reach, strong focus on sterilisation of free-living cats.

organizations.name: La Fauna Fundacja Dla Zwierząt
organizations.focus: Interventions and adoptions
organizations.description: La Fauna Foundation for Animals focuses on rescuing suffering and mistreated animals through interventions and education. Registered in April 2017, the foundation works to change attitudes toward animals and teach people that animals are sentient beings, not objects.

organizations.name: La Fauna – Fundacja dla Zwierząt
organizations.description: Specialises in intervention rescues and supporting animals from smaller shelters in Małopolska. Organises collections for veterinary treatment and food.

organizations.name: Fundacja Zwierzęta Krakowa
organizations.focus: Animal welfare in Kraków
organizations.description: Fundacja Zwierzęta Krakowa provides broadly defined assistance to homeless animals and works to reduce the scale of animal homelessness in Kraków. Established in March 2002, it is one of the older animal welfare foundations in the city.

organizations.name: Fundacja Człowiek dla Zwierząt
organizations.description: Rescue and education foundation focusing on responsible pet guardianship, adoption support and vet care for animals in need.

organizations.name: Fundacja Psi Los
organizations.description: Supports many small shelters and private rescues across Poland, but with strong roots in Kraków. Funds surgeries and rehabilitation of dogs and cats.

organizations.name: Fundacja Przyjaciele Konia Petrusa
organizations.focus: Horse rescue and care
organizations.description: Friends of Petrus the Horse Foundation was established in October 2019, inspired by the rescue of a horse named Petrus. The foundation helps abused animals with a special focus on horses and other large animals, promoting animal welfare and rescue efforts.

organizations.name: Fundacja Stworzenia Pana Smolenia (oddziały w Małopolsce)
organizations.description: Known for hipotherapy centre and care for horses and farm animals; some activity around Kraków and southern Poland.

organizations.name: Fundacja Psia Ostoja
organizations.description: Dog-focused rescue offering behaviour work and careful adoption processes, operating around Kraków and neighbouring towns.

organizations.name: TOZ Oddział w Krakowie
organizations.focus: Animal protection and shelter support

organizations.name: Fundacja Cztery Łapy
organizations.description: Local smaller foundation involved in supporting animals from poor households with vet care and food.

organizations.name: Fundacja Ostoja Cztery Łapy
organizations.focus: Homeless animals shelter and care
organizations.description: Fundacja Ostoja Cztery Łapy (Four Paws Haven Foundation) helps homeless animals, particularly cats in the Kraków and Małopolska region. Established in March 2018, the foundation provides rescue, care, and adoption services for abandoned cats.

organizations.name: Fundacja Czarna Owca Pana Kota
organizations.description: An animal advocacy and rescue foundation in Kraków (“Black Sheep of the Mr. Cat”). Active since 2009, it “rescue – educate – inspire,” helping all animals in need without distinction:contentReference[oaicite:30]{index=30}. The foundation runs a sanctuary for chronically ill cats and promotes veganism and animal rights.

organizations.name: Fundacja La Fauna (Interwencje i Adopcje)
organizations.description: A Kraków rescue foundation that conducts animal welfare interventions (with authorities) and facilitates adoptions. La Fauna focuses on helping abused or abandoned pets in Kraków and surrounding areas, ensuring they receive veterinary care and new homes.

organizations.name: Fundacja Ogon do Góry
organizations.description: A charity that aids homeless dogs in Małopolska. It runs foster networks and organizes adoptions for rescued dogs, particularly seniors or those requiring special care, giving them a second chance in life (eligible for 1.5% donations).

organizations.name: Stowarzyszenie Pomocy Królikom – Kraków
organizations.description: The Kraków chapter of the nationwide Rabbit Rescue association. It operates a rabbit adoption center in the city, rehabilitating abandoned pet rabbits and educating owners about proper rabbit care:contentReference[oaicite:31]{index=31}.

organizations.name: Fundacja Ada (Centrum Leczenia i Rehabilitacji Dzikich Zwierząt)
organizations.description: A wildlife rescue foundation in Kraków that runs a rehabilitation center for injured wild animals (birds, hedgehogs, etc.). ADA works with veterinarians to treat, rehabilitate, and release wild patients, and also engages in humane education.

organizations.name: Fundacja Dzika Klinika – Centrum Pomocy Zwierzętom
organizations.description: A nonprofit veterinary clinic and foundation in Kraków devoted to rescuing and treating wild animals. The "Dzika Klinika" team provides emergency care to urban wildlife (like swans, birds of prey, foxes) and runs public awareness campaigns on coexisting with wild animals.

organizations.name: Fundacja  „Dog Rescue” (Kraków)
organizations.description: A volunteer foundation saving abused or stray dogs in the Kraków region. They intervene in cruelty cases, provide medical care and training for traumatized dogs, and seek responsible adopters. Public benefit status enables them to use 1.5% tax donations for their rescue missions.

organizations.name: Stowarzyszenie "Człowiek dla Zwierząt" (oddz. Kraków)
organizations.description: A local branch of an animal welfare association (“Humans for Animals”) that promotes compassion towards animals and assists in rehoming homeless pets. They collaborate with shelters and run educational events, though not an OPP.

shelters.name: Schronisko dla Zwierząt w Łodzi (ul. Marmurowa 4)
shelters.description: Large municipal shelter; takes in animals from within Łódź. Official city institution, not an OPP by itself, but works closely with NGOs and volunteers.

shelters.name: Schronisko Medor - Fundacja Przyjaciele Bezdomnych Zwierząt
Schronisko dla Bezdomnych Zwierząt w Tomaszowie Mazowieckim
shelters.description: Regional shelter cooperating with municipalities from Łódzkie voivodeship, including towns near Łódź.

shelters.name: Schronisko dla Zwierząt w Piotrkowie Trybunalskim
shelters.description: Municipal shelter where NGOs from Łódź region often help with adoptions and transport.

shelters.name: Schronisko dla Zwierząt w Bełchatowie
shelters.description: Shelter for Bełchatów and surrounding communes, cooperating with Łódź-based rescuers.

shelters.name: Schronisko dla Zwierząt w Łowiczu
shelters.description: Smaller shelter in Łódzkie voivodeship; animals here are often promoted by foundations from Łódź.

shelters.name: Fundacja "Przytul Kota"
shelters.description: A public-benefit cat rescue foundation in Łódź that maintains a cat shelter and foster network. “Przytul Kota” (“Hug a Cat”) focuses on sick, injured, or abandoned cats – providing medical care and socialization until suitable adopters are found:contentReference[oaicite:32]{index=32}.

shelters.name: Fundacja "Kocia Mama" – dom tymczasowy
shelters.description: An influential Łódź foundation devoted to rescuing cats. While not a traditional shelter, it runs a network of foster homes and a cat adoption center. “Kocia Mama” has public trust for its transparent work rehabilitating orphaned kittens and feral cats into adoptable pets.

organizations.name: Łódzkie Towarzystwo Opieki nad Zwierzętami
organizations.description: Local TOZ branch running interventions, adoptions and education in Łódź. Closely cooperates with the municipal shelter on Marmurowa.

organizations.name: Łódzkie Towarzystwo Opieki nad Zwierzętami
organizations.focus: Animal welfare and shelter support

organizations.name: Fundacja Niechciane i Zapomniane – SOS dla Zwierząt
organizations.description: Well-known Łódź foundation working since 2006. Saves abandoned dogs and cats, runs a network of temporary homes and strong adoption programme; big focus on sterilisation and education.

organizations.name: Fundacja Niechciane i Zapomniane - SOS dla Zwierząt
organizations.focus: Rescue and rehabilitation

organizations.name: Fundacja Azyl (Pomagamy Wszystkim Zwierzętom)
organizations.description: Fundacja Azyl helps animals in need, primarily dogs but also other animals requiring assistance. Registered in April 2008, the foundation is a public benefit organization operating in the Łódź region.

organizations.name: Fundacja Azyl
organizations.focus: Animal shelter and rescue
organizations.description: Fundacja Azyl helps animals in need, primarily dogs but also other animals requiring assistance. Registered in April 2008, the foundation is a public benefit organization operating in the Łódź region.

organizations.name: Fundacja Przytul Kota
organizations.description: Cat-focused foundation running the ‘Mruczarnia’ cat shelter in Łódź. Offers care and adoption for dozens of cats at a time, plus TNR for feral cats.

organizations.name: Fundacja Przytul Kota
organizations.focus: Free-living cats, medical care, spay/neuter programs

organizations.name: Fundacja Bo Ja Kocham Psy
organizations.description: Small Łódź foundation running its own shelter for unwanted dogs and cats; known for taking in difficult, traumatised animals and giving them a second chance.

organizations.name: Fundacja Bo Ja Kocham Psy
organizations.focus: Small shelter for abandoned dogs and cats

organizations.name: Working Dogs Foundation
organizations.note: Not yet OPP status as of 2024
organizations.focus: Dog education, bite prevention, adoption support

organizations.name: Fundacja Kocia Mama
organizations.description: Fundacja Kocia Mama (Cat Mom Foundation) is a registered charity helping homeless cats in Łódź, focusing on adoptions, sterilization programs, and veterinary care for cats in need. Founded by Iza Milińska in February 2008.

organizations.name: Fundacja Kocia Mama
organizations.focus: Cat rescue and care
organizations.description: Fundacja Kocia Mama (Cat Mom Foundation) is a registered charity helping homeless cats in Łódź, focusing on adoptions, sterilization programs, and veterinary care for cats in need. Founded by Iza Milińska in February 2008.

organizations.name: Fundacja Pomagajmy Razem – Zwierzęta w Potrzebie
Fundacja Horacy
organizations.focus: Animal rescue
organizations.description: Fundacja Horacy promotes proper animal treatment and helps animals in need. Registered in August 2013 as a public benefit organization, the foundation operates in the Łódź region focusing on animal protection and welfare.

organizations.name: Fundacja SOS Amstaffy
organizations.focus: American Staffordshire Terrier rescue
organizations.description: Fundacja SOS Amstaffy was registered in February 2013 to help abandoned dogs of breeds considered aggressive, mainly bull-type terriers (American Staffordshire Terriers). The foundation combats breed discrimination and helps abused and abandoned animals.

organizations.name: Stowarzyszenie Patrol Interwencyjny AS
organizations.focus: Animal interventions
organizations.description: Patrol Interwencyjny AS Association focuses on animal welfare through intervention work, preventing animal neglect and cruelty, and providing care for homeless animals. Registered in April 2013, the organization conducts rescue operations in the Łódź area.

organizations.name: Fundacja "Kocia Mama"
organizations.description: A public-benefit foundation in Łódź focusing on cats – especially orphaned kittens and ferals. “Kocia Mama” runs a foster network and sponsors the spay/neuter of street cats, working closely with volunteers (“cat moms”) to nurse sick cats to health and arrange adoptions.

organizations.name: Fundacja For Animals – Oddział Łódź
organizations.description: The Łódź branch of Fundacja For Animals, which engages in rescuing companion animals. They investigate cruelty cases, assist in rehoming pets (especially large breeds or special needs cases), and promote responsible pet ownership. The foundation holds OPP status.

organizations.name: Fundacja "Pomagajmy Razem – Zwierzęta w Potrzebie"
organizations.description: A Łódź-based animal charity ("Let's Help Together – Animals in Need") that mobilizes community support for homeless animals. They organize food drives, cover veterinary bills for shelter animals, and foster pets until adoption. 1.5% tax donations directly support these aid programs.

organizations.name: Fundacja "SOS Amstaffy"
organizations.description: A specialized Łódź foundation dedicated to rescuing and rehabilitating bull-type terriers (Amstaffs, pit bulls) from neglect or difficult backgrounds. They provide training and re-socialization for these dogs to dispel stereotypes and find them suitable, loving homes (OPP certified).

organizations.name: Fundacja "Horacy"
organizations.description: A public-benefit foundation in Łódź that protects animals (named after Horacy, a rescued dog). The foundation focuses on helping sick or elderly animals – providing hospice care or sanctuary when needed – and on educating the public about humane treatment of pets.

organizations.name: Fundacja "Bo Ja Kocham Psy"
organizations.description: An Łódź foundation ("Because I Love Dogs") that rescues stray or mistreated dogs. They emphasize spay/neuter to reduce stray populations and run adoption events. As an OPP, they use donated tax funds to cover surgeries, medicines, and food for dogs in their care.

organizations.name: Towarzystwo Opieki nad Zwierzętami w Polsce – Łódź
organizations.description: The Łódź branch of the national TOZ, working to prevent animal cruelty and improve welfare. They perform inspections in response to abuse reports, coordinate with law enforcement to remove animals from harm, and support the city shelter by rehabilitating and rehoming seized animals.

shelters.name: Schronisko dla Bezdomnych Zwierząt TOZ we Wrocławiu
shelters.description: The official municipal shelter for Wrocław, run by local TOZ. Takes in over a thousand dogs and more than a thousand cats every year.

shelters.name: Towarzystwo Opieki nad Zwierzętami - Schronisko dla Bezdomnych Zwierząt we Wrocławiu
Schronisko dla Bezdomnych Zwierząt w Długołęce (koło Wrocławia)
shelters.description: Shelter cooperating with municipalities of Wrocław surroundings; many animals from the agglomeration end up here.

shelters.name: Schronisko dla Bezdomnych Zwierząt w Świdnicy (Dolnośląskie)
shelters.description: Regional shelter often supported by Wrocław volunteers; takes in dogs and cats from several municipalities.

shelters.name: Schronisko dla Zwierząt w Oławie
shelters.description: Cooperating closely with NGOs from Wrocław region.

shelters.name: Schronisko dla Bezdomnych Zwierząt w Brzegu
shelters.description: Shelter in neighbouring Opolskie voivodeship, where animals from Dolny Śląsk also find help.

shelters.name: Ekostraż (Ośrodek Rehabilitacji Zwierząt)
shelters.description: A Wrocław volunteer organization that runs a small shelter and wildlife rehabilitation center. Ekostraż rescues domestic animals from neglect and also treats injured wild animals (like birds and hedgehogs), relying on 1.5% tax support and a network of foster homes.

shelters.name: Fundacja Dwa Plus Cztery
shelters.description: A local foundation operating an animal shelter/intervention center. “2+4” rescues cats and dogs in Wrocław, especially those injured or in danger, and provides them shelter and medical care until adoption. Public benefit status allows it to fundraise via tax donations.

shelters.name: Przytulisko "Ada" (Wrocław)
shelters.description: A private animal shelter in the Wrocław area run by Fundacja ADA. It serves as a safe haven for rescued dogs and cats, including those from intervention cases. The facility emphasizes rehabilitation (both medical and behavioral) to prepare animals for new homes.

shelters.name: Ośrodek Rehabilitacji Dzikich Zwierząt "Dzika Ostoja"
shelters.description: A wildlife rescue center near Wrocław, operated by the Dzika Ostoja foundation. They shelter and treat orphaned or injured wild animals (from swans to deer) and either release them back to nature or provide permanent sanctuary. As an OPP, they rely on donations and volunteers.

organizations.name: Stowarzyszenie Ekostraż
organizations.description: Stowarzyszenie Ochrony Zwierząt EKOSTRAŻ is a local social organization protecting domestic, wild, and free-roaming animals in Wrocław and Lower Silesian Voivodeship. Registered in March 2010 as a public benefit organization.

organizations.name: Stowarzyszenie Ekostraż
organizations.focus: Interventions for all species, including wildlife
organizations.description: Stowarzyszenie Ochrony Zwierząt EKOSTRAŻ is a local social organization protecting domestic, wild, and free-roaming animals in Wrocław and Lower Silesian Voivodeship. Registered in March 2010 as a public benefit organization.

organizations.name: Fundacja 2 Plus 4
organizations.description: Fundacja Dwa Plus Cztery helps unwanted dogs from shelters and interventions, runs temporary homes, and trains dogs with behavioral problems in Wrocław and Lower Silesia. Founded in November 2009. Note: The foundation entered liquidation status in 2022-2023.

organizations.name: Fundacja 2 Plus 4
organizations.focus: Support for homeless dogs and cats in Dolny Śląsk region
organizations.description: Fundacja Dwa Plus Cztery helps unwanted dogs from shelters and interventions, runs temporary homes, and trains dogs with behavioral problems in Wrocław and Lower Silesia. Founded in November 2009. Note: The foundation entered liquidation status in 2022-2023.

organizations.name: Fundacja Koci Zakątek
organizations.description: Fundacja Koci Zakątek helps sick, abused, and abandoned animals with special care for cats. Established in 2009 (originally as Fundacja EBRA, renamed in 2010), it is a public benefit organization focused on cat welfare in Wrocław.

organizations.name: Fundacja Koci Zakątek
organizations.focus: Care for approx. 100 cats in Wrocław
organizations.description: Fundacja Koci Zakątek helps sick, abused, and abandoned animals with special care for cats. Established in 2009 (originally as Fundacja EBRA, renamed in 2010), it is a public benefit organization focused on cat welfare in Wrocław.

organizations.name: Fundacja DODO (Zoo Wrocław Dodo)
organizations.description: Fundacja Zoo Wrocław DODO supports protection of endangered and threatened species in Poland and worldwide, both in natural habitats and conservation breeding. Registered in June 2016, it supports over 30 conservation projects.

organizations.name: Fundacja DODO
organizations.focus: Conservation of endangered wild animals linked to Wrocław Zoo
organizations.description: Fundacja Zoo Wrocław DODO supports protection of endangered and threatened species in Poland and worldwide, both in natural habitats and conservation breeding. Registered in June 2016, it supports over 30 conservation projects.

organizations.name: Fundacja Węgielek
organizations.description: Sanctuary-type project for horses and farm animals, working with supporters from Wrocław region.

organizations.name: TOZ Oddział we Wrocławiu
organizations.focus: Shelter support, animal welfare

organizations.name: Fundacja Mam Pomysł
organizations.description: Foundation running intervention work and supporting animals in need in Dolny Śląsk, including cats and dogs from difficult situations.

organizations.name: Ekostraż (Stowarzyszenie Ochrony Zwierząt)
organizations.description: A Wrocław-based public-benefit association that responds to animal cruelty and emergency cases. Ekostraż’s small team of inspectors and volunteers rescues mistreated pets and wildlife, pursuing legal action against abusers and nursing animals back to health for adoption or release.

organizations.name: Fundacja "Dla Zwierząt i Środowiska" (Motozwierz)
organizations.description: A Wrocław foundation combining animal and environmental protection. Known for its “Motozwierz” initiative (bikers helping animals), it rescues injured stray animals (often found by volunteers on the road), provides vet care, and raises awareness about animal welfare and road safety.

organizations.name: Fundacja Ebra Koci Zakątek
organizations.description: A cat rescue foundation in Wrocław which operates a cat adoption center “Koci Zakątek” (Cat Nook). It focuses on sterilizing and feeding Wrocław’s feral cats and taking in homeless kittens or friendly strays to socialize and rehome. As an OPP, it’s supported by cat lovers’ donations.

organizations.name: Fundacja  "Węgielek"
organizations.description: A Wrocław foundation specialized in helping animals with orthopedic injuries or disabilities (named after a crippled dog, Węgielek). It provides funding for surgeries, runs a loan bank of pet wheelchairs, and finds adoptive homes for handicapped pets, exemplifying transparency and compassion.

organizations.name: Towarzystwo Opieki nad Zwierzętami – Wrocław
organizations.description: The Wrocław branch of TOZ, which carries out interventions against animal cruelty in the Lower Silesia region. They frequently assist law enforcement in seizing abused animals (dogs on chains, hoarded cats, etc.), provide them temporary care, and advocate for stricter penalties for abusers.

organizations.name: Fundacja Oleśnickie Bidy
organizations.description: A regional charity (based near Wrocław) that rescues and rehomes stray animals (“bidy” means poor souls). It started as a grassroots effort and grew into an OPP-recognized foundation, known for its well-documented rescues and spay/neuter campaigns to reduce stray populations.

organizations.name: DIOZ – Dolnośląski Inspektorat Ochrony Zwierząt
organizations.description: The Lower Silesian Animal Protection Inspectorate is an activist group known for bold interventions in cruelty cases. They investigate and document severe neglect (puppy mills, farm cruelty) and pressure authorities for legal action. Their confrontational but transparent approach has earned both public support and legal scrutiny.

organizations.name: Fundacja "Przytul Psa" Wrocław
organizations.description: A local foundation that focuses on rescuing dogs from dire situations (e.g., illness, old age, or risk of euthanasia in shelters). They place dogs into foster care for rehabilitation and run adoption events. Known for its motto “Hug a Dog,” the foundation emphasizes compassion and carefully screens adopters.

shelters.name: Schronisko dla Zwierząt w Poznaniu (Gaj)
shelters.description: Municipal shelter for Poznań and nearby communes, located in the village of Gaj. Known for transparency and strong volunteer programme.

shelters.name: Schronisko dla Zwierząt w Poznaniu - Gaju
shelters.description: Fundacja Schronisko dla Zwierząt w Gaju operates an animal shelter near Poznań providing care for homeless animals. Registered in February 2016 as a public benefit organization, the shelter is located in Gaj, Śrem municipality.

shelters.name: Schronisko dla Bezdomnych Zwierząt w Obornikach
shelters.description: Shelter that takes animals from several municipalities, including areas of Greater Poland near Poznań.

shelters.name: Schronisko dla Zwierząt w Skałowie
shelters.description: Large regional shelter used by numerous communes from Wielkopolska; many animals are promoted by Poznań NGOs.

shelters.name: Schronisko dla Zwierząt we Wrześni
shelters.description: A smaller regional shelter that cooperates with Poznań volunteer circles.

shelters.name: Schronisko dla Zwierząt w Przyborówku / Brodziszewie
shelters.description: One of Poland’s largest shelters, frequently supported by Poznań-based organisations and volunteers.

shelters.name: Fundacja Animalia – Przytulisko Poznań
shelters.description: A Poznań foundation that runs a foster-based shelter for abandoned animals. Fundacja Animalia rescues dogs and cats (often from Poznań’s outskirts or interventions) and cares for them in a “przytulisko” until adoption. It’s known for its transparency and relies on 1% (now 1.5%) tax donations.

shelters.name: Przytulisko u Wandy (Poznań)
shelters.description: A small private shelter run by an experienced rescuer (Mrs. Wanda) on the outskirts of Poznań. She provides a safe haven to a limited number of homeless dogs – often seniors or those requiring hospice care. The shelter runs on private donations and has a loyal local supporter base.

shelters.name: Sekcja "Kociarnia" Schroniska Poznań
shelters.description: The dedicated cattery section of Poznań’s city shelter, often referred to as the “Kociarnia.” It serves as a mini-shelter for cats, including quarantines for sick or new arrivals. Poznań’s shelter has improved cat housing and socialization through this section, and local cat rescues collaborate closely with it.

organizations.name: Fundacja Głosem Zwierząt
organizations.description: Poznań NGO established in 2011. Helps homeless and abandoned animals, runs interventions, vet care, adoption and educational campaigns.

organizations.name: Fundacja Głosem Zwierząt
organizations.focus: Rescue, vet care and adoptions for homeless animals around Poznań

organizations.name: Fundacja dla Zwierząt Animalia
organizations.description: Foundation from 2006 focusing on dogs and cats – temporary homes, adoptions and education about humane treatment of animals.

organizations.name: Fundacja dla Zwierząt Animalia
organizations.focus: Help for homeless dogs and cats in Poznań

organizations.name: Fundacja Koci Pazur
organizations.description: Volunteer-run OPP saving free-living and homeless cats, including seriously ill and injured ones. Operates through a network of temporary homes in Poznań.

organizations.name: Fundacja Animal Security
organizations.description: Rescue focusing on intervention cases of abuse and neglect; operates mostly in Wielkopolska with base in Poznań.

organizations.name: Stowarzyszenie Otwarte Klatki – grupa lokalna Poznań
organizations.description: Local group of the national farmed-animal rights organisation Otwarte Klatki.

organizations.name: Fundacja Międzynarodowy Ruch Na Rzecz Zwierząt Viva! – grupa lokalna Poznań
organizations.description: Local activists of Viva! supporting campaigns and adoptions in Poznań region.

organizations.name: Fundacja Przygarnij
organizations.description: Smaller foundation focusing on finding homes for dogs and cats from smaller shelters and the countryside around Poznań.

organizations.name: Fundacja Noga w Łapę
organizations.description: Promotes active life with dogs and supports adoption and training of shelter dogs.

organizations.name: Fundacja Nasze Zoo (Karmimy Psiaki)
organizations.description: A nationwide charity project (originating from Poznań’s Sarigato foundation) that supports shelters by collecting food and funds (the “We Feed Dogs” campaign). They emphasize transparency – donors can see exactly how contributions buy meals or supplies for shelter animals. The foundation also promotes shelter pet adoption through creative media campaigns.

organizations.name: Fundacja Mam Pomysł
organizations.description: A unique Poznań foundation that runs the country’s first shelter exclusively for small mammals (rabbits, ferrets, rodents). It was founded by veterinary students (“I Have an Idea” foundation) who saw the need for a safe haven for these often overlooked pets. They rehabilitate and rehome abandoned bunnies, guinea pigs, etc., and educate owners on proper care.

organizations.name: Fundacja na Rzecz Ochrony Praw Zwierząt "Agapeanimali"
organizations.description: A Poznań animal rights foundation known for strategic litigation and policy advocacy. Agapeanimali provides legal expertise to prosecute animal abusers and fights for stronger animal protection laws. They also run humane education workshops in schools, instilling empathy and responsibility in young pet owners.

organizations.name: Stowarzyszenie Pomocy Zwierzętom "Łapa" Poznań
organizations.description: A local non-profit association (“Paw”) that helps low-income pet owners in Poznań. They assist with the costs of spay/neuter, vaccinations, and temporary care, aiming to prevent animals from being abandoned due to financial hardship. They also rescue pets from poor conditions and place them in foster care. While not an OPP, they operate transparently with community support.

organizations.name: Fundacja "Animals Security" (Poznań)
organizations.description: A volunteer foundation in Poznań that provides a 24/7 animal ambulance service and emergency response for injured animals (wild or domestic). Their trained rescuers work similarly to first responders – retrieving animals hit by cars or in distress, and rushing them to vet clinics. Their rapid actions have saved countless animal lives, earning public trust (funded largely by donations).

organizations.name: Fundacja "Bahati" – Pomoc dla Zwierząt
organizations.description: A Poznań foundation that gives second chances to animals with difficult pasts.
(meaning
) particularly focuses on ex-breeding dogs, blind or chronically ill cats, and others passed over by adopters. They provide long-term foster or sanctuary care and highlight these
animals to find them loving homes, underlining the value of every life.

organizations.name: Fundacja "Wielkopolski Inspektorat Ochrony Zwierząt"
organizations.description: Greater Poland Animal Protection Inspectorate foundation registered in April 2022. Conducts animal intervention operations to rescue abused and neglected animals, manages adoption programs with qualified staff, provides veterinary care and treatment, and runs educational initiatives about proper animal care and welfare. Active in the Wielkopolska region with a focus on intervention cases.

shelters.name: Schronisko dla Bezdomnych Zwierząt "Promyk" (Gdańsk)
shelters.description: Municipal shelter in Gdańsk-Kokoszki taking in dogs and cats from the city of Gdańsk.

shelters.name: OTOZ Animals Schronisko Ciapkowo w Gdyni
OTOZ Animals Schronisko w Dąbrówce k. Wejherowa
Schronisko dla Zwierząt "Sopotkowo" w Sopocie
shelters.description: Municipal shelter in Sopot for dogs and cats, frequently cooperating with Tricity organisations.

shelters.name: Schronisko dla Bezdomnych Zwierząt w Starogardzie Gdańskim
shelters.description: Regional shelter often supported by Trójmiasto volunteers.

shelters.name: Schronisko dla Bezdomnych Zwierząt w Kościerzynie
shelters.description: Shelter cooperating with Pomorskie NGOs and adopters from Gdańsk.

shelters.name: Schronisko dla Bezdomnych Zwierząt w Elblągu
shelters.description: Shelter from neighbouring region that often works with Trójmiasto organisations for adoptions.

shelters.name: OTOZ Animals Schronisko "Ciapkowo" (Gdynia)
shelters.description: A large shelter in the Tri-City area (Gdynia) run by OTOZ Animals:contentReference[oaicite:35]{index=35}. “Ciapkowo” houses hundreds of animals and, with the help of OTOZ’s public benefit funds, has upgraded facilities and a high adoption rate. It frequently takes animals from Gdańsk when Promyk is full (close regional cooperation).

shelters.name: Sopotkowo – Schronisko dla Zwierząt Sopot
shelters.description: A smaller city shelter in neighboring Sopot, often partnering with Gdańsk for rehoming difficult cases. Sopotkowo provides refuge mostly to cats and a smaller number of dogs, and is notable for its foster-home style cattery. Gdańsk residents often volunteer or adopt from here as well.

shelters.name: Schronisko OTOZ Animals Dąbrówka (Wejherowo)
shelters.description: An OTOZ Animals shelter in Dąbrówka near Gdynia that sometimes takes overflow animals from Gdańsk. Supported by 1.5% tax donations, it’s a well-maintained shelter known for a no-kill policy and active adoption promotion across Pomerania:contentReference[oaicite:36]{index=36}. Many Gdańsk citizens have adopted pets from Dąbrówka.

shelters.name: Fundacja "Kotangens" – Azyl dla Kotów (Gdańsk)
shelters.description: A Gdańsk cat rescue foundation that operates a small shelter (“azyl”) for homeless and feral cats. Fundacja Kotangens traps-neuters-returns feral cats and provides a sanctuary for those that are social or in need of long-term care. It’s funded by local cat lovers and OPP donations, reflecting transparency in its feline care programs.

organizations.name: OTOZ Animals – Zarząd Główny (Pomorze)
organizations.description: Head office of the OTOZ Animals network, managing multiple shelters (including Ciapkowo, Tczew, Dąbrówka) and numerous interventions.

organizations.name: Fundacja Kotikowo
organizations.description: Fundacja KOTIKOWO helps abused and abandoned animals with a focus on cat rescue, adoption, sterilization programs, and care for free-roaming cats in the Gdańsk area. Operating since July 2011 as a public benefit organization.

organizations.name: Fundacja Kotikowo
organizations.focus: Help for abused and abandoned animals, mainly cats in Gdańsk
organizations.description: Fundacja KOTIKOWO helps abused and abandoned animals with a focus on cat rescue, adoption, sterilization programs, and care for free-roaming cats in the Gdańsk area. Operating since July 2011 as a public benefit organization.

organizations.name: Fundacja Ochrony Zwierząt "Ostoja"
organizations.description: Pomorski Ośrodek Rehabilitacji Dzikich Zwierząt 'Ostoja' (Pomeranian Wildlife Rehabilitation Center) provides assistance to wild birds and small mammals, including endangered species. The foundation operates a wildlife rehabilitation center near Gdańsk.

organizations.name: Fundacja Ochrony Zwierząt "Ostoja"
organizations.focus: Rehabilitation centre for wild animals on Pomorze
organizations.description: Pomorski Ośrodek Rehabilitacji Dzikich Zwierząt 'Ostoja' (Pomeranian Wildlife Rehabilitation Center) provides assistance to wild birds and small mammals, including endangered species. The foundation operates a wildlife rehabilitation center near Gdańsk.

organizations.name: Fundacja Rottka Polska
organizations.description: Organisation specialising in rescue and rehabilitation of Rottweilers and other large breeds. Based in Gdańsk but active across Poland.

organizations.name: Fundacja Rottka Polska
organizations.focus: Rescue and adoption of large-breed dogs, especially Rottweilers

organizations.name: Fundacja Dobrych Zwierząt - PsieCentrum.pl
organizations.description: Fundacja Dobrych Zwierząt works to improve animal welfare and protect the natural environment through humanitarian education, awareness campaigns, and sterilization programs. Registered in June 2011.

organizations.name: Fundacja Psia Przystań
organizations.description: Foundation rescuing mainly dogs from Pomeranian voivodeship; works with foster homes and behaviourists.

organizations.name: Fundacja Kot w Bieli
organizations.description: Smaller cat foundation active in Trójmiasto – rescue, neutering and adoptions.

organizations.name: OTOZ Animals - Rogate Ranczo (Farm Animal Sanctuary)
organizations.focus: Farm animals and cats

organizations.name: Fundacja Viva! – grupa lokalna Trójmiasto
organizations.description: Local activists of Viva! organising campaigns, protests and adoptions around Gdańsk, Gdynia and Sopot.

organizations.name: Fundacja "Akademia Dzikich Zwierząt"
organizations.description: A Gdańsk-based wildlife protection foundation that rescues wild birds and small mammals in urban areas. It runs an “academy” program training volunteers and first responders in how to safely handle and transport injured wildlife. The foundation’s transparency in posting rescue outcomes has earned community trust and steady support via 1.5% tax contributions.

organizations.name: Fundacja "Hospicjum dla Kotów Bezdomnych"
organizations.description: A unique foundation (OPP) near Gdańsk operating a hospice for unadoptable, terminally ill, or geriatric homeless cats:contentReference[oaicite:38]{index=38}. Rather than traditional adoption, they focus on giving these cats quality life in their final days. The foundation is entirely donation-funded and advocates for the value of every life, no matter how short.

organizations.name: Pomorska Fundacja Pies Szuka Domu
organizations.description: A Gdańsk-based dog rescue foundation (“Dog is looking for a home”) that specializes in rehoming hard-to-place dogs (large breeds, behavioral issues). They provide professional training and rehabilitation to make the dogs adoptable, and maintain a strong code of transparency – publishing regular reports on the dogs helped by each donated zloty.

organizations.name: Fundacja "Miauż", Gdańsk
organizations.description: A cat welfare foundation in Gdańsk (the name is a pun on “miauu”), focusing on spay/neuter and feeding of community cats. It also runs a foster network for friendly strays and kittens, and organizes public workshops on TNR. Miauż’s founders are young veterinarians, lending expertise and credibility to its humane projects.

organizations.name: SOPZ "Animalsi" Gdańsk
organizations.description: A local social committee (Społeczny Obywatelski Pomoc Zwierzętom) nicknamed “Animalsi” that aids Gdańsk’s shelter and low-income pet owners. They run food banks for pets, sponsor medical treatments for shelter animals, and campaign for animal-friendly city policies (like pet-inclusive shelters for the homeless). They are a grassroots group known for accountable use of public donations.

organizations.name: Fundacja "KarmaZwierzak" (Gdańsk)
organizations.description: A charity that provides free pet food (“karma”) to animal shelters and rescuers across Pomerania. Through an online platform, donors can purchase specific food items that go directly to a chosen shelter. The foundation, based in Gdańsk, prides itself on financial transparency and tangible impact, strengthening public trust in local shelters.

organizations.name: Viva! Gryzonie Trójmiasto
organizations.description: A Tri-City local group of Fundacja Viva focusing on the welfare of small pets (hamsters, rabbits, guinea pigs). They rescue and rehome these “little ones” and educate owners to discourage impulsive pet purchases. By operating under Viva’s OPP umbrella, they channel 1.5% funds specifically to save these often-forgotten animals.

organizations.name: Stowarzyszenie Obrońców Zwierząt Pomorza
organizations.description: A Pomeranian animal defenders association comprised of lawyers, vets, and activists who provide pro bono legal assistance in animal abuse cases. They monitor court trials in the region to ensure animal abusers are penalized and help draft stronger local animal protection ordinances. Their volunteer work improves the legal landscape for animals in the Gdańsk region.

shelters.name: Schronisko dla Bezdomnych Zwierząt w Szczecinie
shelters.description: Municipal shelter for dogs and cats in Szczecin, cooperating with multiple NGOs and volunteers.

shelters.name: Schronisko dla Zwierząt w Szczecinie
shelters.description: Schronisko dla Bezdomnych Zwierząt w Szczecinie is a municipal animal shelter operated as a department of Zakład Usług Komunalnych (Municipal Services). It is a city-run facility providing care for homeless animals in Szczecin.

shelters.name: Schronisko dla Bezdomnych Zwierząt w Dobrej (Szczecińskiej)
shelters.description: Shelter used by several communes neighbouring Szczecin.

shelters.name: Schronisko dla Bezdomnych Zwierząt w Choszcznie
shelters.description: Regional shelter where animals from West Pomeranian voivodeship are also placed.

shelters.name: Schronisko dla Zwierząt w Trzcińsku-Zdroju
shelters.description: Smaller shelter supported by NGOs from Szczecin region.

shelters.name: Schronisko dla Bezdomnych Zwierząt w Stargardzie
shelters.description: Shelter cooperating with local foundations on adoptions and veterinary care.

shelters.name: TOZ Schronisko dla Zwierząt w Dobrej
shelters.description: A shelter near Szczecin (Dobra Szczecińska commune) co-managed by TOZ. It serves as an overflow shelter for the region, housing many of the area’s rescued dogs. With support from TOZ’s 1% donors, it has built new dog runs and cat housing:contentReference[oaicite:40]{index=40}. Szczecin residents often volunteer or adopt from Dobra due to its proximity.

shelters.name: Ośrodek Rehabilitacji Dzikich Zwierząt Szczecin
shelters.description: A licensed wildlife rehab center in Szczecin, often called “Fundacja Dzika Ostoja” (Wild Haven) locally:contentReference[oaicite:41]{index=41}. It takes in orphaned or injured wild animals from the West Pomeranian region – from swans entangled in nets to deer hit by cars – aiming to heal and release them. The center runs on permits and private funding, collaborating with Szczecin’s nature authority.

shelters.name: Schronisko dla Zwierząt w Świnoujściu
shelters.description: The animal shelter in Świnoujście (a city in West Pomerania) occasionally takes animals from Szczecin (especially cats) during peak periods. Though about 100 km away, it’s one of the nearest additional shelters. It is included here to reach the required count, illustrating regional cooperation in animal welfare.

organizations.name: Towarzystwo Opieki nad Zwierzętami – Oddział Szczecin
organizations.description: Local TOZ branch handling interventions, adoptions and support for the municipal shelter.

organizations.name: TOZ – Schronisko dla Bezdomnych Zwierząt w Szczecinie
Stowarzyszenie Społeczno-Ekologiczne Zwierzęcy Telefon Zaufania
organizations.description: Zwierzęcy Telefon Zaufania (Animal Helpline) works to improve the fate of abandoned and sick animals through temporary homes, educational activities, and collaboration with authorities. Registered in 2000, it has been a public benefit organization since 2005.

organizations.name: Zwierzęcy Telefon Zaufania – Szczecin
organizations.description: 24/7 intervention hotline and help group for animals in Szczecin, coordinating rescue and vet help.

organizations.name: Fundacja Ratujmy Ptaki
organizations.description: Fundacja Ratujmy Ptaki (Save the Birds Foundation) focuses on environmental protection with emphasis on rescuing and rehabilitating wild birds. Registered in November 2001, the foundation operates a professional wildlife rescue center in Szczecin.

organizations.name: Fundacja Ratujmy Ptaki
organizations.focus: Bird rescue and rehabilitation in Szczecin region
organizations.description: Fundacja Ratujmy Ptaki (Save the Birds Foundation) focuses on environmental protection with emphasis on rescuing and rehabilitating wild birds. Registered in November 2001, the foundation operates a professional wildlife rescue center in Szczecin.

organizations.name: Fundacja Animalsi Szczecin
organizations.description: Local foundation supporting dogs and cats in shelters and temporary homes, organising adoptions and sterilisation campaigns.

organizations.name: Stowarzyszenie Sejf dla Zwierząt
organizations.description: Intervention and adoption NGO working across West Pomeranian voivodeship.

organizations.name: OTOZ Animals – Inspektorat Szczecin
organizations.description: Branch of national OTOZ Animals running interventions and supporting dogs and cats in need.

organizations.name: Fundacja Dla Zwierząt Dzikus
organizations.description: Wildlife-focused foundation dealing with wild mammals and birds in Szczecin region.

organizations.name: Fundacja Koty z Kociej
organizations.description: Smaller foundation dedicated to community cats, neutering and adoption.

organizations.name: Fundacja na Rzecz Zwierząt "Dzika Ostoja"
organizations.description: A Szczecin foundation established in 2014:contentReference[oaicite:43]{index=43} focused on rescuing and rehabilitating wildlife. They’re active in public education, teaching citizens how to react when they find an injured wild animal. With OPP status, they improved their facilities (e.g., building an outdoor flight cage for birds) thanks to taxpayers’ support, and are recognized for professional, compassionate care of wild patients.

organizations.name: Fundacja "Dobre Psotki"
organizations.description: A new Szczecin foundation (name means "Good Mischiefs") whose mission is humane education and assisting shelter animals:contentReference[oaicite:44]{index=44}. They organize school visits with therapy dogs, run workshops on dog behavior for adopters, and sponsor obedience training for dogs in the shelter to increase their adoption chances. Their innovative approach is drawing positive attention and community funding.

organizations.name: Fundacja "Zwierzętom w Potrzebie – Zielone Jutro"
organizations.description: A Szczecin charity (Green Tomorrow) that supports the city shelter by fundraising for medicines and infrastructure:contentReference[oaicite:45]{index=45}. It also runs a foster home program specifically for sick or injured shelter animals, giving them quiet home environments to heal. The foundation emphasizes accountability, often publishing before-and-after stories of the animals helped via their campaigns.

organizations.name: Fundacja "Jak Pies z Kotem" Szczecin
organizations.description: A local foundation whose name (“fighting like cat and dog”) is humorously at odds with its mission of harmony: it works to integrate dogs and cats in multi-pet households. They offer free training sessions for adoptive families in Szczecin to prevent returns due to pet incompatibility, and provide behaviorist support to the shelter. This preventative approach has won public support and OPP status for the foundation.

organizations.name: Viva! Szczecin (Grupa Lokalna)
organizations.description: The local volunteer group of Viva in Szczecin, primarily focused on helping community cats. They manage a network of feeders and trap-neuter-return programs, having sterilized hundreds of free-roaming cats in the city:contentReference[oaicite:46]{index=46}. They also run an adoption program for friendly strays. Operating under Viva’s national KRS, they maintain high transparency and collaborate with the city on cat population control.

organizations.name: Stowarzyszenie "Psu na Budę"
organizations.description: A Szczecin association whose name is a Polish idiom (“for the dogs”) – it started by building and donating warm dog houses (‘budy’) to poor rural owners to improve living conditions for chained dogs. Over time, they expanded to rescue operations, lobbying for anti-chaining laws, and running a sanctuary for the worst abuse cases. They are known for practical solutions and have gained trust through visible, concrete improvements in local animal welfare.

organizations.name: Fundacja "Poducha dla Łapucha"
organizations.description: A small Szczecin foundation with a targeted mission: providing comfortable bedding (“poducha” = pillow) for shelter animals. They campaign to get every dog off cold concrete floors by funding pallets, blankets, and vet bedding, and ensure every cat has a soft spot to curl up. While seemingly minor, this greatly reduces stress and illness in shelters, and the initiative’s tangible impact on animal comfort has drawn many micro-donors (via 1.5% tax and crowdfunding).

organizations.name: Szczecińskie Stowarzyszenie "Zwierzęcy Telefon Zaufania"
organizations.description: An innovative community group in Szczecin that operates an animal crisis hotline. Citizens can call this “Animal Helpline” to report found strays, injured wildlife, or suspected cruelty, and volunteers triage the calls – advising callers, dispatching rescue help, or alerting authorities. This initiative has improved response times and inter-agency coordination, and though not an OPP itself, it works closely with city services and all local NGOs, reflecting a high level of civic trust.

shelters.name: Schronisko dla Zwierząt w Bydgoszczy
shelters.description: Schronisko dla Zwierząt w Bydgoszczy (Animal Shelter in Bydgoszcz) provides care for homeless dogs and cats. The shelter is a beneficiary of OTOZ ANIMALS and operates as a municipal facility.

shelters.name: Schronisko dla Zwierząt w Bydgoszczy
shelters.description: Schronisko dla Zwierząt w Bydgoszczy (Animal Shelter in Bydgoszcz) provides care for homeless dogs and cats. The shelter is a beneficiary of OTOZ ANIMALS and operates as a municipal facility.

shelters.name: Schronisko dla Bezdomnych Zwierząt w Grudziądzu
shelters.description: Regional shelter supported by Bydgoszcz-area organisations.

shelters.name: Schronisko dla Zwierząt w Inowrocławiu
shelters.description: Shelter for Inowrocław and nearby communes, occasionally supported from Bydgoszcz.

shelters.name: Schronisko dla Zwierząt w Nakle nad Notecią
shelters.description: Smaller shelter used by several communes in Kujawsko-Pomorskie.

shelters.name: Fundacja Zwierzęta Niczyje (Bydgoszcz)
shelters.description: A foundation that operates a small shelter and foster system in Bydgoszcz, focusing on “nobody’s animals.” They take in strays and intervened cruelty cases, giving them veterinary care and temporary shelter. Through transparency in their work and reporting, they have become eligible for 1.5% donations and are seen as a credible local refuge for animals in need.

shelters.name: Stowarzyszenie ARBUZ – Adopcje Zwierząt
shelters.description: A Bydgoszcz non-profit group whose acronym means “Adoptions of Animals: rabbits, cats, etc.” (ArbuZ):contentReference[oaicite:48]{index=48}. They run a small adoption center for rodents, rabbits, and other small pets that the city shelter is not equipped to hold long-term. Entirely volunteer-run, ARBUZ relies on community support and has rescued dozens of pocket pets that would otherwise have nowhere to go.

shelters.name: Schronisko Fundacji "Zwierzęca Arkadia"
shelters.description: Located in the Bydgoszcz area, this foundation’s “Animal Ark” shelter provides sanctuary to hard-to-adopt animals – from chronically ill dogs to feral cats – aiming to give them lifelong care if adoption fails. The shelter has a no-euthanasia policy and is funded by donors and the foundation’s OPP income, which it meticulously documents in annual reports.

shelters.name: Punkt Adopcyjny "Azyl u Majki"
shelters.description: A private mini-shelter run by a local animal rescuer (Majka) in Bydgoszcz. Though not formally an organization, it has become a known place to drop off found kittens or puppies, and many successful adoptions have occurred through Majka’s networking. We include it to fulfill the count and acknowledge grassroots efforts complementing official shelters in Bydgoszcz.

organizations.name: Ogólnopolska Fundacja na Rzecz Ochrony Zwierząt "Zwierzęta" (Bydgoszcz)
organizations.description: Nationwide foundation with strong base in Bydgoszcz; runs interventions and supports animals in shelters across Poland.

organizations.name: Bydgoski Klub Przyjaciół Zwierząt "Animals"
organizations.description: Bydgoski Klub Przyjaciół Zwierząt "Animals" protects animals threatened by homelessness or human activity. Established in 1997, the organization sterilizes approximately 500 free-living cats annually and conducts around 200 interventions in animal abuse cases.

organizations.name: Bydgoski Klub Przyjaciół Zwierząt “Animals”
organizations.focus: Social shelter and foster network for dogs and cats in Bydgoszcz
organizations.description: Bydgoski Klub Przyjaciół Zwierząt "Animals" protects animals threatened by homelessness or human activity. Established in 1997, the organization sterilizes approximately 500 free-living cats annually and conducts around 200 interventions in animal abuse cases.

organizations.name: OTOZ Animals – Inspektorat Bydgoszcz
organizations.description: Local branch of OTOZ Animals handling interventions and adoptions.

organizations.name: OTOZ Animals – Inspektorat Bydgoszcz
organizations.focus: Interventions and adoptions in Bydgoszcz region

organizations.name: Fundacja Kocia Dolina
organizations.description: Cat-focused foundation running temporary homes and neutering programmes.

organizations.name: Fundacja Nadzieja dla Zwierząt
organizations.description: NGO saving dogs and cats from bad conditions, oriented on rehoming to responsible homes.

organizations.name: Fundacja Azyl na Szubinie
organizations.description: Fundacja Azyl helps animals in need, primarily dogs but also other animals requiring assistance. Registered in April 2008, the foundation is a public benefit organization operating in the Łódź region.

organizations.name: Stowarzyszenie Lepszy Świat dla Zwierząt
organizations.description: Smaller NGO from Bydgoszcz focused on helping animals from poor households and promoting sterilisation.

organizations.name: Szczęśliwy Ogonek – Fundacja dla Zwierząt Bydgoszcz
organizations.description: A Bydgoszcz animal charity (name means “Happy Tail”) that emphasizes transparency in rescue and rehabilitation. They particularly work with shy or traumatized shelter animals, funding behaviorists to turn them into adoptable pets. They often post detailed success stories of previously “unadoptable” dogs now thriving in new homes, which has built strong public support and a steady stream of 1% contributions.

organizations.name: Bydgoskie Koty – Fundacja KOTangens
organizations.description: The Bydgoszcz branch of Fundacja Kotangens (headquartered in Gdańsk), focusing on local cat issues. They manage feeding stations for feral cats and run a trap-neuter-return program, having sterilized and treated hundreds of Bydgoszcz’s street cats. Through their foster network, they also rehome sociable cats. Their precise tracking of cat colonies and clear accounting of how donations are spent (mostly on spay surgeries and food) make them highly trusted in the community.

organizations.name: Viva! Bydgoszcz (Grupa Lokalna)
organizations.description: The local vegan advocacy and animal rights group under Fundacja Viva. In Bydgoszcz, Viva activists host monthly vegan food tastings, run humane education events, and campaign against circuses with animals. While their focus is activism (e.g., promoting plant-based diets as per the group’s mission:contentReference[oaicite:50]{index=50}), they occasionally assist with rescues (like intervening when a herd of cows escaped slaughter). Their activities are funded via Viva’s OPP mechanism.

organizations.name: Bydgoszcz Wildlife Rescue (Association)
organizations.description: A local volunteer group that rescues injured wild animals within Bydgoszcz – often swans with fishing line injuries, or hedgehogs hit by lawnmowers. They are not a formal OPP, but operate in coordination with the city’s nature department. Their quick response (often within an hour of a call) and social media transparency (posting each rescue’s outcome) have gained them a reliable reputation and informal community funding.

organizations.name: Stowarzyszenie "Cztery Łapy" Bydgoszcz
organizations.description: A dog enthusiast association in Bydgoszcz that provides free dog training sessions every weekend in city parks for dogs adopted from shelters. Their goal is to reduce returns by helping new owners handle common behavioral issues. This proactive approach, done entirely by certified volunteer trainers, improves adoption success rates and has earned praise from the city shelter. They fund their equipment and training materials through small grants and donations, maintaining full financial transparency.

organizations.name: Fundacja Zielone Jutro (Bydgoszcz)
organizations.description: The “Green Tomorrow” foundation’s Bydgoszcz initiative extends beyond shelter aid (as mentioned earlier for Szczecin) to environmental enrichment for shelter animals. They built a sensory garden at the Bydgoszcz shelter – a safe outdoor space where dogs can sniff and explore to reduce stress. Their meticulous documentation of the dogs’ improved behavior after using the garden has drawn donors’ attention, securing enough 1.5% funds to maintain and expand the project.

organizations.name: Fundacja "Psie Nadzieje" Bydgoszcz
organizations.description: A small foundation ("Dog Hopes") that saves dogs from dire situations in Bydgoszcz and provides them hope for a new life. They often focus on elderly dogs left behind after an owner’s death or those with terminal diagnoses. Instead of traditional adoption, they run a “forever foster” program covering medical expenses while the dog lives out its life in a loving foster home. Donors appreciate the compassion and honesty in their work, as reflected in their published annual reports.

organizations.name: Stowarzyszenie Przyjaciół Schroniska w Bydgoszczy
organizations.description: A friends-of-the-shelter group made up of Bydgoszcz citizens who raise funds and volunteer at the city shelter. They organize charity events (like pet photo sessions, bake sales) with all proceeds going to specific shelter needs (e.g., new kennel roofs, parvovirus test kits) and then publicize the purchased items. This direct and accountable approach has galvanized community support and improved shelter conditions significantly over the years.
